scope_statement: TWO-REGIME SCOPE. The RNA family-DEFINITION (E_r homology) operates cleanly in the DIVERGENT regime (core_recip < ~0.80): copies are aligner-resolvable, O1(definition) is the operative task, and the genuine residual FP is single-conserved-domain over-merge (~66%% of that regime's FP mass = 1141/1729, ~21%% of all its edges, largely non-segdup -- this is where the true residual FP lives). The NEAR-IDENTICAL regime (core_recip > ~0.90) is the ASSIGNMENT regime (O2): copies collapse/confuse, and the apparent E_p 'FPs' are dominated by E_p-OVER-SPLIT-of-real-duplications (colinear>=2, all SEDEF-confirmed) + CARDINALITY (over-counted near-identical copies) -- truth-artifacts, not genuine over-merges -- so the raw E_p FP rate OVERSTATES real over-merges (corrected precision 0.97). The O1->O2 HANDOFF sits at core_recip ~0.70-0.80 (FP-composition flip + corrected-precision saturation), co-located with the shipped O1 purity floor (0.80) but DISTINCT from and BELOW the O2 read-confusability boundary (0.90 core_recip / 0.99 per-segment). O2 assignment machinery (per-read PSV/SUN) is needed above ~0.99 per-segment identity. HONEST CAVEAT: this two-regime split holds on the WHOLE-COPY axis (core_recip); on the requested per-SEGMENT axis (mean_matched_id) it is contaminated by confusability (raw precision dips at 0.95-0.99 and re-spikes to 34 single-domain over-merges at 100%% segment id), independently reproducing 'confusability is per-segment, not a family property'.
